pr_body:
he `afterRender` hooks currently run after `ApplicationRef.tick` but
also run after any call to `ChangeDetectorRef.detectChanges`. This is
problematic because code which uses `afterRender` cannot expect the
component it's registered from to be rendered when the callback
executes. If there is a call to `ChangeDetectorRef.detectChanges` before
the global change detection, that will cause the hooks to run earlier
than expected.

This behavior is somewhat of a blocker for the zoneless project. There
is plenty of application code that do things like `setTimeout(() =>
doSomethingThatExpectsComponentToBeRendered())`, `NgZone.onStable(() =>
...)` or `ApplicationRef.onStable...`. `ApplicationRef.onStable`
should likely work similarly, but all of these are really wanting an API
that is `afterRender` with the requirement that the hook runs after the
global render, not an individual CDRef instance.

This change updates the `afterRender` hooks to only run when
`ApplicationRef.tick` happens.

fixes https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/52429
fixes https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/53232

issue_context.title: Add option to `afterRender*` hooks to only run on global change detection
issue_context.body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

core

### Description

The `afterRender` and `afterNextRender` hooks currently trigger on _any_ change detection. This could include a call to `ChangeDetectorRef.detectChanges`. There is no way to create a render hook that only runs when the global change detection is triggered (i.e. `ApplicationRef.tick`). 

This is especially problematic for `afterNextRender` when the intent is almost always to run after the next global change detection or "after rendering _this_ component". The problem is that there might be a `ChangeDetectorRef.detectChanges` call before the global `ApplicationRef.tick` might happen. This would mean that the component may not have been change detected/rendered when the hook runs.

### Proposed solution

Add a property to the `AfterRenderOptions` to only run the hook after a _global_ change detection (`ApplicationRef.tick`) rather than running it on _any_ change detection (`ChangeDetectorRef.detectChanges`).

### Alternatives considered

There's no alternative at the moment.
comments: Note: current thinking is that `afterRender` should do this by default.

review_comments: Should we test that the `view.checkNoChanges()` don't throw instead? Not sure if the recursive tick() call is covering this already.

Do you mean that it does throw? i.e. a test covering the new `checkNoChanges` after running the `afterRender`* hooks? That test exists here: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/packages/core/test/acceptance/change_detection_signals_in_zones_spec.ts#L892

Just clarifying: an end user doesn't need to jump through all of these hoops to test applications with `afterRender`, right? If they do, I think it might be worth reevaluating this approach. But if it just works, then it's probably fine.

Great question. This was something we discussed in a recent team meeting. A lot of the changes to these tests are because they're asserting exact counts and timings that would be confusing with how it works in `ComponentFixture`. Specifically the assertions on 0 calls are not exactly possible with the fixture because `createComponent` causes `ApplicationRef.tick` to happen, which executes the callbacks. 

For the `ComponentFixture` case and user tests, the hooks _will_ run when `fixture.detectChanges` is called because that has an `NgZone.run` call in it which will also cause `ApplicationRef.tick` to happen. The timing isn't always synchronous but it will happen eventually (`fixture.whenStable` can be used for cases that have a `Promise` and will run hooks asynchronously). This timing "problem" is expected and generally preferred. If we chose to execute the hooks synchronously at the end of `detectChanges`, it would mean that tests would cause the hooks to flush with a different timing than they do in the application.

I added a test with `ComponentFixture` as well to cover this.
